method: greedy randomized construction over the dispatching rules FIFO, MOR, SPT and MWKR under the exact mask: at each dispatch the candidates whose rule score is within alpha times the range of the scores of the legal pairs of the best score, one drawn uniformly (SPT: a pair; FIFO, MOR, MWKR: a job, which goes to its legal machine with the shortest processing time); worker w takes rule (w + j) mod 4 for its sample j and alpha uniformly from 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3; sample 0 of workers 0 to 3 is the deterministic rule FIFO, MOR, SPT, MWKR in turn (p86_extend_scale_sets.masked_rollout), worker 0 taking the rules of missing workers; 8 single-thread workers
statistics: p94.compare_at and p94.compare (p94.stat_instance: stats_family.instance_boot, fresh default_rng(7) per quantity; stats_family.direction), p94.mark_held, p94.verdict_at (p94.verdict_family: instance_boot draws, stats_family.boot_p_one_sided, stats_family.holm, p94.selected_verdict)

comparisons.rnd_vs_pol: the randomized rules minus the policy's greedy schedule, in percent of the greedy schedule (the form of the decision table)
comparisons.smp_vs_rnd: the policy's sampled schedules minus the randomized rules
comparisons.rnd_vs_rule: the randomized rules minus the best of the four deterministic rules
comparisons.mem_vs_rnd: the best of the eight memetic runs started from the rule schedule minus the randomized rules
comparisons.cp_vs_rnd: CP-SAT (8 workers) started from the rule schedule minus the randomized rules

smp_vs_rnd.rule: ahead: the instance-level 95% interval lies below zero and the Holm-adjusted one-sided bootstrap p for "the policy is shorter" (draws of that interval) is below alpha; behind: the interval lies above zero and the Holm-adjusted one-sided bootstrap p for "the policy is longer" (its own Holm family) is below alpha; not distinguishable otherwise. No seed-level test exists for one run.
